title: Delight and will: the inside of the Keser, and of the soul
overview:
The chapter opens the *Keser* in particular. It is the intermediary: its inside, *Atik*, is the last level of the emanator, removed from "the days of the world"; its outside, *Arich*, is the head of the emanated. What they are is delight and will.

Which is inside which? There is no will without a delight in it, and an angry child spits out the ice cream he loves because he doesn't want it. So neither has existence without the other: they are one essence, not two friends that never part. The soul runs after every pleasure and shrinks from pain just as far, so its essence looks like delight, and the early Kabbalists said nothing is higher than delight. It is not so: the essence is higher, though delight is so close that knowing a person's delight is almost knowing him. The clearer proof is that delight keeps every power alive: the kind man, the cruel, the Olympic contender, the thinker. And without will there is no delight. In a discussion after the chapter, Rabbi Markel ties this to the levels of *teshuva* and to the *Akeida*, where Avraham changed the very essence of his kindness.

terms.gloss: the Ancient of Days; the inside of the Keser, removed from the days of the world, the end of the Ein Sof
delight; as the essence of the soul, the capacity to feel pleasure and the need for it
will; the whole soul running after a thing
existence, what keeps a thing going; neither will nor delight has it without the other
composite: a delight or will in a separate thing, which the soul is pulled after though it is not the soul's own ("it's an ice cream")
pleasure; oneg hamurkav, a composite pleasure
pain, sorrow; the opposite of oneg, which lessens the soul's light, its life force
the essence of the soul; it seems to be delight, and is really higher
a word that means either will or delight, because they are one thing
the Ancient of the Ancients; here, a person's self-perception, which is both a will and a delight
self-sacrifice; here mesirus haratzon, giving up the will of the very essence of one's midda

sections.title: The Keser as the intermediary: Atik above, Arich the head of what is emanated
sections.summary: The *Keser* is the interface between the emanator and the emanated: its inside is part of the *ma'atzil*, its outside the head of *Atzilus*. *Atik* is removed from the days of the world; *Arich* is the beginning of the emanated, though the two count as one.

phrases.he: (כג) והנה בפרטיות בחינת הכתר, איך שהוא בחינת ממוצע
phrases.en: It's an intermediary, an interface.

phrases.he: ויש בו מבחינת האחרונה שבמאציל, והוא בפנימיות שבו,
phrases.en: The inside of it is part of the *ma'atzil*,

phrases.he: והוא שרש וראש לנאצלים בחיצוניות שבו,
phrases.en: and the outside is the head of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בעץ חיים

blocks.text: The *Keser* (crown) is the *memutza*, the intermediary. **The inside of it is part of the *ma'atzil*** (the one who emanates), its last level, and **the outside is the head of *Atzilus*** (the world of Emanation), the head of what is emanated, as the *Etz Chaim* explains.

phrases.he: וגם היות ידוע שבחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין מובדל ומרומם, בלתי מלובש בנאצלים
phrases.en: The three *mochin* of *Atik* are totally *muvdal* from the *ne'etzalim*.

phrases.he: וזהו המתנשא מימיות עולם
phrases.en: Higher than the days of the world.

phrases.he: ולכך נקרא עתיק יומין,
phrases.en: Removed from the days. That's why he's called *Atik*.

phrases.he: מלשון המעתיק הרים כו',
phrases.en: Who tears up, tears off the mountain.

phrases.he: שנעתק מימות עולם כו'.
phrases.en: He's totally removed from the days of the world, meaning from the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: הנה כל זה ידוע.
phrases.en: This is all known.

blocks.text: The three *mochin* (intellectual faculties) of *Atik Yomin* (the Ancient of Days) are not dressed in what is emanated: "exalted above the days of the world", here meaning *Atzilus*, though earlier *Atik* itself was the days of the world. Everything is in relationship.
**Removed from the days**: that is why it is called *Atik*, removed, as in "who uproots mountains", tears them off. All this is known.

phrases.he: ויש להבין בזה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: We have to explain in a particular way:

phrases.he: בהיות שעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין נחשב לאחד,
phrases.en: it's really considered one thing.

phrases.he: רק שבכללות נחשב בחינת עתיק יומין מסוף עולם האין סוף, ובחינת אריך אנפין הוא שרש וראש לנאצלים,
phrases.en: In general, *Atik* is the end of the *Ein Sof*, and *Arich* is the beginning of the *ne'etzalim*,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים.

blocks.text: More particularly, *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* (the long countenance) are one thing; only in general is *Atik* the end of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite) and *Arich* the head of the emanated.

sections.title: Delight and will: each looks like the inside of the other
sections.summary: *Atik* and *Arich* are delight and will. There is no will without a delight in it, and no delight in what one does not want, so each seems to be the inside of the other. The conclusion: they are one essence, not two friends that never part, whether in the soul's own simple delight or in a composite one.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע שזהו בחינת התענוג והרצון
ולהיות שאנו רואים שבכל רצון יש תענוג, ולולי התענוג לא היה רצון לדבר כלל
כמו הרצון לעושר וכבוד, לולי שיש בו תענוג לא היה רוצה בזה כלל
אם כן התענוג הוא בחינת פנימיות הרצון לכאורה
phrases.en: So at first glance it looks like the *taanug* is the *pnimiyus* of the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: They are *taanug* (delight) and *ratzon* (will). A will for anything is there only because of the delight in it. **So at first glance it looks like the *taanug* is the *pnimiyus* of the *ratzon***, its inner side.

phrases.he: ואנו רואים להיפוך גם כן,
phrases.en: We see also the opposite:

phrases.he: שאם אין רצון אין תענוג
שהרי דבר שלא ירצה בו לא יתענג ממנו כלל.
phrases.en: If you don't want something, there won't be a *taanug*.

phrases.he: אם כן הרצון פנימית התענוג

blocks.title: The angry child and the ice cream
blocks.text: **We see also the opposite**: a child in a rage, offered ice cream, screams that he doesn't want it; force it down his throat and he spits it out, though he loves ice cream. **If you don't want something, there won't be a *taanug*.**

So the will is the inside of the delight. Otherwise everybody would want every delight there is: everybody would be a drug addict, and everybody would be fat. Getting drunk is a very definite *taanug*, yet to a person who has no *ratzon* for it, it is the opposite of one.

blocks.question: Maybe some people simply take no delight in getting drunk, and it has nothing to do with their will?
blocks.text: No. There is a physical *taanug* in it, and not only for some people: it raises your dopamine. Ice cream is a physical *taanug* too. All kinds of things have *taanug*, and not everybody wants every one, because of the will.

phrases.he: ואנו רואים שזה בלא זה אינו מתקיים,
phrases.en: You can't have a *kiyum* of *ratzon* without a *taanug*, or *taanug* without *ratzon*:

phrases.he: כי אין לרצון קיום בלא תענוג ואין לתענוג קיום בלא רצון
phrases.en: There's no *ratzon* without a *taanug* and no *taanug* without a *ratzon*.

phrases.he: ולפי זה מוכרח לומר ששניהם מהות אחד,
phrases.en: Really they're *mamash* one thing, not like *chachma* and *bina*,

phrases.he: מאחר שמאמצעות חיבורם יחד דוקא יתקיים כו'
phrases.en: It's only when they're both together then there can be an actual *ratzon* and *taanug*.

blocks.text: So sometimes the will is inside the delight. **There's no *ratzon* without a *taanug* and no *taanug* without a *ratzon***: neither has *kiyum* (existence) alone.

blocks.title: The woman watching her weight
blocks.text: A woman worried about her weight won't enjoy the ice cream: she feels so guilty eating it, because her will is against it. But that will has a delight too: it comes from the delight she would get from being thin. You can never tell which is on the inside and which on the outside.

So they are *mamash* one thing. *Chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) are "two friends that never part", but two; will and delight are not two at all. **It's only when they're both together then there can be an actual *ratzon* and *taanug*.**

phrases.he: וכל זה בין בתענוג ורצון פשוט ועצמי,
phrases.en: Whether it's in a *taanug* and *ratzon atzmi* of the soul itself, the *hiyuli ratzon* and *taanug*,

phrases.he: בין בתענוג ורצון מורכב
phrases.en: *murkav*, meaning from something: not the actual inner desire and *taanug* of the soul,

phrases.he: שהנפש מתפשט ונמשך אחריו,
phrases.en: but it's just that the *nefesh* is pulled after it.

phrases.he: גם שאינו מעצמותה, אלא הוא דבר נבדל כו'.
phrases.en: It's not actually the *Atzmus* of the soul; it's an ice cream.

blocks.text: All this holds in the soul's own *hiyuli* (raw, formless) will and delight, up to G-d's own *Atzmus* (essence) and down to a delight of *kelipa* (the husk that hides G-dliness).

Even a delight in something actually bad, beyond *kelipas noga* (lit. the glowing husk). A composite delight, *murkav*, is not the soul's own; the soul is only pulled after it, like a kid after a lollipop. It is a separate thing: **it's an ice cream**.

sections.title: The soul runs after delight and flees pain, so its essence looks like delight
sections.summary: The soul is drawn after any pleasure, even a composite one, and shrinks from pain exactly as much as it expands in joy. So the essence of the soul seems to be delight, the capacity for and need of pleasure, and the early Kabbalists said there is nothing higher than delight.

phrases.he: ואמנם בכלל אנו רואים שהנפש טבעה להתמשך אחר דבר שיש בו תענוג,
phrases.en: The nature of the soul is to be pulled after something that has a *taanug*

phrases.he: עד שיכול להיות כל עצמותה נמשך ונכלל בו
כעונג המורכב בפרט נבדל,
phrases.en: even with an *oneg hamurkav* in a separate thing, meaning something separate from it,

phrases.he: כמו בכבוד או ממון
phrases.en: like people are pulled after honor or money,

phrases.he: או חכמה,
phrases.en: like some people are pulled after various kinds of intellectual pursuits,

phrases.he: ומדות בחסד ודין
phrases.en: like some people are pulled after *chesed*, and like the Romans were pulled after *achzariyus*;

phrases.he: וניצוח
phrases.en: some people, their whole pleasure is to win;

phrases.he: והתפארות
phrases.en: *shvitzing*, showing off.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
או בדברים שהנפש מחמדתן, כתאוות כל תענוגי העולם הזה
phrases.en: *Mamash* physical things, even down to *treif taanugim*.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: By nature the soul is pulled after anything with a *taanug*, until its whole self is drawn into it. See a little kid, or a dog that *mamash* pulls on his leash till he chokes.

Even with *oneg hamurkav* (a composite pleasure), in a thing separate from the soul: honor, money, intellectual pursuits, *chesed* (kindness), or, like the Romans, *achzariyus* (cruelty); winning; *shvitzing*, showing off. Any of these *middos* (emotional attributes) can be holy or *kelipa*.
Or all the pleasures of this world, *mamash* physical things, even down to *treif* (not kosher) pleasures. That is their whole problem: the *taanug* in them pulls the soul after them.

phrases.he: אף על פי שכל אלה אינן בבחינת עצמיות התענוג ההיולי, רק שהנפש תומשך ותחמוד להם,
אבל מזה נראה שעצם הנפש הוא בבחינת תענוג ההיולי
phrases.en: The *etzem hanefesh* is in a way of a *taanug*; that's what it wants. It is made up of a desire for *taanug*.

phrases.he: על כן תומשך אחר עונג מורכב ותברח מן הצער, שהוא היפך העונג
phrases.en: It by nature runs after any kind of *oneg*, even *oneg hamurkav*, and runs away from the opposite of *oneg*, *tzaar*.

blocks.text: None of these is the *hiyuli* delight; the soul only covets them. But it shows that the *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul) is made of a desire for delight, so it runs after any pleasure, even a composite one, and away from *tzaar* (pain).

phrases.he: עד שב' קוין שקולין הן ממש
phrases.en: How much the *oneg* is in something, that's how much the *tzaar* is from its opposite.

phrases.he: שכפי ערך התפשטות הנפש במלאת אורה בדברי תענוג,
phrases.en: How much the *nefesh* gets filled up with the *taanug*,

phrases.he: כן תתכווץ ותתמעט אורה בצער ויגון בתכלית כו'
phrases.en: that's how much it'll get *mismaet*, its light.

blocks.text: The two pans of the scale weigh the same. As chapter six explains, at the airport people cry at a parting as much as they enjoy an arrival. **How much the *oneg* is in something, that's how much the *tzaar* is from its opposite.**
As far as the soul's light, its *chayus* (life force), spreads out in delight, so far it shrinks in pain and sorrow.

blocks.title: Jumping for joy, dying of a broken heart
blocks.text: A big win and a person can't stand still; he jumps up and down. A big loss, *chas v'shalom* (Heaven forbid), and he is so depressed he won't talk to anyone; one can even die of a broken heart, as has been seen in animals that lost a mate or young.

phrases.he: ומזה נראה בעצם מהותה, שהוא התענוג
phrases.en: The *etzem mahus* of the soul is *taanug*.

phrases.he: והעיקר ממה
phrases.en: And the main thing that you see it from, even more than the fact that it runs after *taanug*:

phrases.he: שתברח ותתכווץ מן הצער
phrases.en: that the soul will run away and will get lessened from sorrow.

phrases.he: מזה ראיה יותר כו'
phrases.en: This is an even bigger proof.

blocks.text: So the *mahus* (being) of the soul is *taanug*: the capacity for pleasure and the need for it. The main sign is that it runs from sorrow and shrinks from it, more than that it runs after delight. **This is an even bigger proof.**
A person will do anything to escape *tzaar*. That, in fact, is how dictators get people to do what they want: they threaten them with *tzaar*.

phrases.he: ועל כן גזרו אומר המקובלים הראשונים,
phrases.en: That's why the *mekubalim harishonim* said

phrases.he: שהתענוג נחשב מעצם הנפש,
phrases.en: the *taanug* is *mamash* the *etzem hanefesh*.

phrases.he: ואמרו שאין לך למעלה מן העונג
phrases.en: They said there's nothing higher than *oneg*.

blocks.text: That is why the early *mekubalim* (Kabbalists) said delight is the very essence of the soul, and nothing is higher than *oneg* (pleasure). Kabbalistic books call *Atik* the *Atzmus*, and in many places call the *Keser* the essence of the soul.

But this is not really what they meant: delight is so close to the essence that knowing a person's delight, you basically know his soul. The essence is higher, "and not of any of these attributes at all", surely the *Atzmus* of the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). Still, will and delight are all you need to know.

So with the *mitzvos*: studying *halacha* is in one way higher than *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) or *Kabbala*, though in another they are higher, because there, as the *Tanya* explains, you know the essence of the will.

blocks.title: Tacos on a shidduch
blocks.text: Even a composite thing shows will and delight. On a *shidduch* (a match), people find out what movies and foods the other likes. Who cares if they like tacos and you don't? But by finding out what they like and want, you find out about them.

So with the *Aibershter*: the *halachos* deal with external things, sometimes a mere "if" (*korbanos*, sacrifices, need a *Beis HaMikdash*), yet knowing His will and delight is like knowing Him. That is what the *mekubalim* meant.

Still, it is not really so: the soul itself, and the *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof*, are higher than the *Kesarim* (crowns), higher than simple delight. Delight is only close enough that knowing it is almost enough.

sections.title: Not so: the essence is higher, and is only drawn into delight and pain
sections.summary: The essence of the soul is not delight. It is drawn after a great delight with its whole self until it almost expires into it, and in extreme sorrow it expires for lack of light.

phrases.he: ואין האמת כן,
phrases.en: But it's not really like that.

phrases.he: רק שהעצמיות דנפש תתמלא מן התענוג הרב ותומשך כל עצמותה, עד שתכלה ותומשך כמעט כולה,
phrases.en: It all gets pulled after the thing.

phrases.he: כמו כלתה נפשי כו'
phrases.en: My whole soul is finished up in this *ratzon* and *taanug*.

blocks.text: In truth the soul is drawn after a great delight with its whole self, until it almost expires into it, like a little kid screaming for what he wants. Great delight can make one faint: *tzaddikim* (the righteous) actually fainted, and emotional people faint at seeing a loved one after many years.

phrases.he: ולהיפך תכלה בגרעון אור לגמרי
phrases.en: And the opposite also: the soul will be finished off with no light at all left, to the point that, *chas v'shalom*, a person can actually die,

phrases.he: מכל וכל, מעוצם הצער המופלג כידוע

blocks.text: And extreme sorrow can leave the soul with no light at all, until, *chas v'shalom*, a person can die: someone who lost a person he loved, or a man into money who lost it all.

sections.title: The clearer proof: delight keeps each power alive, from kindness to wisdom
sections.summary: In every particular power of the soul, the delight in it is what keeps it in existence: the kind man lives on the pleasure of doing good, the cruel on the pleasure of cruelty, the contender on winning, and the thinker on the joy of a new idea.

phrases.he: וראיה ברורה יותר
phrases.en: And an even clearer proof for this:

phrases.he: ממה שאנו רואים שגם בפרטי כחות של הנפש, הנה בחינת העונג שבזה הכח בפרטות, הוא עיקר קיום מציאותו תמיד
phrases.en: in the particular *kochos*, the *sefiros* in other words, the *oneg* in this thing is the main *kiyum* of its *metzius*.

phrases.he: כמו הכח של מדת החסד, גם שהוא עצמי וטבעי בטבע הטוב להטיב,
phrases.en: The *midda* is *atzmi*, same like *chesed*, a *midda atzmi*.

phrases.he: עיקר קיומו הוא התענוג, שמתענג בשפע הטוב
phrases.en: The main *kiyum* is the *oneg* that he gets a pleasure from doing good, from doing favors for people.

phrases.he: וזהו קיום האמיתי לטבעיות טובו, שהוא מה שטבעו להתענג ביותר מן ההטבה, עד שכל עיקר חיותו בנפשו בא על ידי עונג זה שבטוב וחסד

blocks.text: An even clearer proof: in each particular power of the soul, the *sefiros* in other words, the delight in that power is the main *kiyum* of its existence.
Take *chesed*, an essential *midda*, natural to the good: still, its main *kiyum* is the pleasure of doing favors, like *Avraham Avinu* (Abraham our father) sitting and waiting to do a *chesed*.

phrases.he: ולהיפוך במי שהוא אכזרי בטבעו, אין זה רק שזהו כל חיותו בתענוג זה שעושה רע ואכזריות, כידוע

blocks.text: The opposite is easier to see, he says: a cruel man lives by the pleasure of cruelty. The Romans' circuses were places of enjoyment; the whole of their cruelty was that they enjoyed it.

phrases.he: וכן במדת הניצוח, כל עיקר קיומו רק העונג המופלג,
phrases.en: The whole *kiyum* of the thing is the *oneg* that they're going to get out of winning,

phrases.he: עד שחיות נפשו נמשך כולה בזה שינצח לזולתו
phrases.en: so that his whole *chayus* of his soul, his whole life

phrases.he: ואם לא ינצח יחלה כו'
phrases.en: If he doesn't win, he can *mamash* get actually sick from it.

blocks.title: The Olympic contender
blocks.text: So with winning: at an Olympic gold, or a football team's win, everybody jumps up and down. **The whole *kiyum* of the thing is the *oneg* that they're going to get out of winning**. Some contenders have no life, no friends, no family, no parties; they just want to win. Someone who only wanted the money could not win the Olympics; his desire would not be strong enough.
And if he does not win, he can *mamash* get sick from it. In contests like skating, when someone loses or stumbles, you see him *mamash* droop.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בכל פרטי פרטי המדות
phrases.en: Not only in the *middos*: in the *pratei pratei hamiddos*, even in the *middos* of the *middos*,

phrases.he: עד החכמה והרצון
phrases.en: even the *chachma* and the *ratzon* itself.

phrases.he: הרי עיקר קיומם ומקורם העונג, ולולי העונג שבהשכלה אין לו כח לחדש שום חכמה,
phrases.en: If not the *oneg* in *haskala*, he wouldn't have a power to be *mechadesh* any *chachma*,

phrases.he: כנראה בחוש
phrases.en: like we actually see this.

blocks.text: So in all the particulars of the *middos*, up to *chachma* and will: their *kiyum* is delight. Without delight in *haskala* (intellectual grasp), no new *chachma* comes. Look at absent-minded philosophers: that is their *taanug*.

blocks.title: The professor and the money-maker
blocks.text: Another man with as big a brain has his *taanug* in making money, so he is full of sharp ideas for it. Why does the absent-minded professor, so smart, have no money, while a fellow with half his brains has it all? Because that one *mamash* enjoys making money.

blocks.title: "That is my enjoyment"
blocks.text: Not that he needs it: some have enough for ten lifetimes and want more. Tell a man closing a ten-million-dollar deal that with a hundred million he should go enjoy Hawaii, and he answers, "That is my enjoyment." That gives the *midda* its *kiyum*.

phrases.he: וכמו שאמר אלמלא חדווה דשמעתא כו'
phrases.en: If not for the pleasure that I got out of the *shmaata*, I could not make a *chiddush*.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין חכמת אדם תאיר פניו,
phrases.en: A person that is interested in *chachma*, when he hears a *chiddush* of *chachma* or he gets a *chiddush* of *chachma*, it *mamash* lights up his face.

phrases.he: שהלחלוחית, שבו עונג ההיולי, הוא המקור להשכיל כל שכל כו'
phrases.en: The *taanug* is the *makor* of the *haskala*.

blocks.text: As was said, "were it not for the joy of the teaching": **If not for the pleasure that I got out of the *shmaata*, I could not make a *chiddush*** (a new insight). He does not remember which rabbi said it.

As "a man's wisdom lights up his face": a new *chiddush* *mamash* lights up the face of someone into *chachma*. The *lachluchis* (moisture) on the brain holds the *hiyuli* delight; as the *Tanya* says, all delights come from the element of water. **The *taanug* is the *makor* of the *haskala*.**

sections.title: And without will there is no delight
sections.summary: From the other side, a man finds no delight in a kindness, a judgement, an idea, a victory or a pleasure of this world that he does not want, which is why one person delights in what leaves another cold.

phrases.he: ואמנם ברצון בלבד אנו רואים שבלא רצון אין תענוג
phrases.en: If not for the *ratzon*, it wouldn't be a *taanug*.

phrases.he: נמצא, גם בכל פרטי המדות
phrases.en: This also is in every *pratei hamiddos*.

phrases.he: כמו אם לא ירצה בחסד או דין אין לו בו תענוג כלל
phrases.en: If he doesn't want a certain *chesed* or a certain *din*, then he won't have a *taanug*.

blocks.text: As for will: without it there is no delight, in every particular *midda* too. **If he doesn't want a certain *chesed* or a certain *din*, then he won't have a *taanug*.** It is the child in a tantrum again: "You love ice cream!" "Not now."

phrases.he: וכן אם לא ירצה להשכיל
phrases.en: Somebody doesn't want to be *maskil*:

phrases.he: לא ימצא העונג לזה כלל
phrases.en: he won't get an *oneg* from it.

phrases.he: וכן אם לא ירצה בניצוח כלל אין לו תענוג בניצוח או התפארות, וכן בשאר תענוגי עולם הזה, כממון וכבוד וכהאי גוונא
בלא רצון אין תענוג בהן כלל וכלל

blocks.text: Someone who does not want to be a *maskil* (a person of intellect) gets no *oneg* from it: tell a bored person to do a crossword puzzle, and if he doesn't want to, he won't enjoy it.

So with winning, showing off, money and honor: without will, no delight. That is why one person delights where another does not. Rock stars delight in fame; a shy person doesn't want it, though everybody would shout for him. Clearer still: ice cream is a delight for everybody, and some people don't want it.

sections.title: Both are needed, because they are one essence
sections.summary: Will, like delight, is the whole soul drawn after a thing, so the two are one essence: their absence is pain, what goes against the will hurts, and no one can say which comes first or which is inside. The word *chafetz* means both.

phrases.he: והיינו מפני שכללות ענין זה הוא בהיות שכל עיקר עצם הנפש נמשך אחר התענוג והרצון,
(שהרצון הוא גם כן המשכת כל הנפש
phrases.en: The *ratzon*, that when you want something, means your whole soul is running after this thing,

phrases.he: עד שכולה תכלה ברצון לדבר מה כו׳ כידוע)
phrases.en: a person wants something, his whole soul goes after it.

phrases.he: על כן גם בכל פרטי כחותיה, עיקר קיומם הוא התענוג והרצון
phrases.en: So therefore, in every particular *kochos*, in the particulars of the particulars, the *ratzon* and the *taanug* is the main *kiyum*.

blocks.text: The general reason: the soul is drawn after delight and will alike. Want something and your whole soul runs after it. So they are *mamash* the same pull of the soul, and in every particular power they are the main *kiyum*.

phrases.he: והעדרם הוא הצער מדבר זה, היפך העונג
phrases.en: When you have a *tzaar* from this thing, then you don't have this *midda*; you have the opposite of this *midda*.

phrases.he: ודבר המנגד לרצון,
phrases.en: Something that's against his *ratzon*,

phrases.he: גם שאינו צער,
phrases.en: even though it's not a *tzaar*,

phrases.he: יצטער ממילא
phrases.en: because he has a *ratzon* against it, it'll make it a *tzaar*.

blocks.text: Their absence is *tzaar*. **When you have a *tzaar* from this thing, then you don't have this *midda*; you have the opposite of this *midda*.**

blocks.title: Ice cream in his face
blocks.text: A thing against the will becomes a pain though it is none in itself: shove ice cream in the face of the child who won't eat it and he gets madder. Right now he has a will against it, so it is a *tzaar*.

phrases.he: כמו אם ירצה לאהוב שונאו,
phrases.en: If he'll want to love his enemy,

phrases.he: יתענג ממנו
phrases.en: they'll get a big pleasure out of it.

phrases.he: ולהיפך אם לא ירצה באהובו,
יצטער ממנו
phrases.en: They will get a *tzaar* from it.

phrases.he: וכן אם יתענג בשנאוי לו המזיקו, ירצה בו,
phrases.en: Because of the great *taanug* they get from it, they nonetheless want it.

phrases.he: ואם יצטער באהוב לו, לא ירצה
phrases.en: Something that he really wants, but he gets a *tzaar* from it, he doesn't want it.

blocks.text: **If he'll want to love his enemy**, he takes pleasure in him. Like these idiots who go to shake hands with Arafat: they come back so glad, such a big *taanug*, that they got to meet Arafat and shook his hand. Idiot, what changed? He's your enemy. But since they want to love their enemy, they get a big pleasure out of it.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the people who went to meet Arafat idiots: a jab at a political camp, about a named figure.
sensitivity.publishable: **If he'll want to love his enemy**, he takes pleasure in him. Like the guys who go to shake hands with Arafat: they come back so glad, such a big *taanug*, that they got to meet Arafat and shook his hand. But what changed? He's your enemy. But since they want to love their enemy, they get a big pleasure out of it.

blocks.text: And if he does not want the one he loves, it pains him: people who love each other can be mad for a moment and not want to see the other, and then **they will get a *tzaar* from it**. That is the will.
And if he delights in something that harms him, he wants it: most drug addicts know it is destroying them, but **because of the great *taanug* they get from it, they nonetheless want it**.

blocks.title: A body like Schwarzenegger
blocks.text: If something he wants pains him, he won't want it. Many want a body like Schwarzenegger's; diet and exercise would give them a great one. So why not? "What, I'm going to eat brown rice?" For him it is the opposite of pleasure.

phrases.he: כי מהות אחד הן הרצון והתענוג,
phrases.en: Because really it's one *mahus*, it's *mamash* one thing.

phrases.he: ולא נודע מי קדם
phrases.en: You *mamash* don't know which is first.

phrases.he: ולפעמים זה פנימי וזה חיצוני, ולפעמים להיפך
phrases.en: Sometimes this is on the inside and this is on the outside, and sometimes the opposite.

phrases.he: ולא ימצא אחד בלא זולתו,
phrases.en: He can't find one without the other.

phrases.he: שאם אין תענוג אין רצון,
phrases.en: Not that they don't work separately, but they're *mamash* not there.

phrases.he: ואם אין רצון אין תענוג
בין בפשוט בין במורכב כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:
phrases.en: This is whether in a *pashut* or a *murkav*; this applies in anything.

blocks.text: For will and delight are *mamash* one thing. **You *mamash* don't know which is first**: sometimes one is on the inside and sometimes the other. Not that they don't work separately, but without the other it is *mamash* not there.

Simple or composite, it is one thing. Hence *chafetz*: in chapter 10, among the *middos* of the *Atzmus*, he says not *chesed* but *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness). *Chafetz* can mean will, as in *chafatzti*, I want, or delight, because they are really the same.

blocks.question: Is that why a *baal teshuva* (one who returns) can overcome what he was drawn after: the inside of *Atik* and *Arich* is affected by *Atika d'Atikin*, a hidden will?
blocks.text: A person's delight comes out of his self-perception, both a will and a delight, called *Atika d'Atikin*. Yes, that is why there can be a *baal teshuva*, though his hidden will was different before: he has to change *Adam Kadmon* (the primordial man), his self-perception, perhaps even his *ratzon kadum* (the primordial will). As was said last time, *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice) can turn the essence of evil into the essence of good; that is how there is *iskafya* (subduing the evil).

These are the levels of *teshuva* (return); *Derech Chaim*, which the class is also learning, ties in closely with this book. Some only realize that what they were into did not fit their self-perception, a *shtus* (foolishness) they fooled themselves with. Others have to *mamash* change it.

Even then the whole self-perception may not change: not the *ratzon l'ratzon* (the will for a will), not even the will itself, only its applications. He wants exactly what he wanted before; he just realized this is not what will get it for him. That is the lower level, where only the action changes: *teshuva tata'a* (the lower return).

Many *baalei teshuva* in America were not really against *Yiddishkeit*. Even one who became a Christian may not need such a high *teshuva*: he wanted the truth, to serve the *Aibershter*, and thought to get there as a spiritual person, like the hippies. Many hippies suddenly became Lubavitchers, and they are still the same hippies. They only realized you get it as a Lubavitcher, not a hippie, through *Yiddishkeit*, not Hinduism.

sensitivity.reason: Teases the hippies who became Lubavitchers as "still the same hippies" and sets Christianity and Hinduism against Yiddishkeit.

blocks.text: Then there are higher levels: some must change up to *chachma*, since the intellect fooled them; then up to *Atik*, then *Adam Kadmon*; then the *ratzon kadum* itself, the desire before the self-perception; and then the very *hiyuli middos* of the soul.

That is hardly possible except through studying *Chassidus*, with *mesirus nefesh* to the *Atzmus*, which is higher than delight: the "it is not truly so". It can change even the delight of the inner *middos*. Generally those cannot change, only their nature, from physical to divine; through *mesirus nefesh* even that changes.

blocks.title: The Akeida changed the essence of the midda
blocks.text: A *gevura* (might) person stays one, and so a *chesed* person: Yitzchak is *gevura*, but divine, and Avraham *chesed*, but divine. The whole point of the *Akeida* (the binding of Isaac) was that Avraham *mamash* changed the *etzem hamidda*, the essence of his attribute, from *chesed* to *din*.

blocks.title: Why the Akeida, not the fire, was the biggest test
blocks.text: Even among *goyim* some will sacrifice their children. The *Akeida* showed that he, the very *ish chesed* (man of kindness), could change the essence of his *midda*: that is why it was the biggest test. Being thrown into the fire himself changed nothing in his *midda*, so it did not prove *mesirus nefesh* into the *Atzmus*. *Mesirus nefesh* is *mesirus haratzon*: giving up the will of the essence of his *midda*.

sensitivity.reason: Says in passing that even among non-Jews some are willing to sacrifice their children.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the inside of the *Keser* and what is its outside, and how do *Atik* and *Arich* divide between them?
How do the angry child and the woman watching her weight show that will and delight have no existence without each other?
Why is the soul's shrinking from pain an even bigger proof than its running after pleasure that its essence looks like delight?
If the essence of the soul is higher than delight, what did the early *mekubalim* mean, and what does it have to do with learning *halacha*?
How do the Olympic contender and the money-maker show that delight keeps a *midda* in existence?
Why are will and delight not like *chachma* and *bina*, and what does the word *chafetz* show?
